- licence/regulatory: RDSO/CLW-approved indigenous IGBT-based 3-phase propulsion equipment for 6,000 HP locomotives — evidence: developed in compliance with CLW standards in September 2025, with commercial supplies to Indian Railways initiated in March 2026 — against it: commercial supplies only began in March 2026, so the approved product has a short supply record

- customer lock-in: established approved-supplier relationship with Indian Railways — evidence: association since 2009 with a validated compliance and certification history; 76.16% of FY2026 revenue derived from Indian Railways — against it: the same 76.16% is a single-customer concentration
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on Government railway spending and procurement programmes — The Company flags changes in Government spending priorities, tendering and procurement processes and dependence on customer procurement programmes as risks to its railway-focused business.
- Long development and customer approval cycles — The railway industry involves long development cycles, stringent approvals and customer approval cycles; regulatory complexity and delays in approvals, land acquisition and project permissions can push out schedules and raise operating costs.
- Safety, reliability and standards compliance — Propulsion equipment and cable assemblies must meet rigorous safety and environmental standards and consistently high reliability; failure can cause project delays, higher costs and reputational damage.
- Intense competition for railway contracts — Numerous domestic and international players bid for contracts, and many competitors have strong ties with Indian Railways.
- Supply-chain disruption and electronic component availability/pricing — Raw materials and components come through a global supply chain exposed to geopolitical tensions, natural disasters or pandemics; availability and pricing of critical electronic components can delay production and raise costs.
- Technology change — The Company lists technology changes in the railway sector among its risks, which it seeks to mitigate through continued R&D and product diversification.

outlook.body:
- Evolve from a supplier of railway electrical products into an advanced propulsion-technology company, built on the approved indigenous locomotive propulsion system.
- Scale up manufacturing operations to strengthen production capacity, supply-chain resilience and support larger propulsion and rail electrical programmes, complemented by investment in engineering, testing, quality systems, automation and skilled talent.
- Broaden the product and technology portfolio beyond locomotive propulsion into trainsets, distributed power propulsion platforms and other next-generation railway applications, supported by the dedicated R&D Centre.
- Keep indigenous, in-house R&D central: the DSIR-recognised R&D Centre is to be strengthened to develop new products and support long-term growth.
- Deploy IPO proceeds towards operational requirements and investment in research, design and development.

outlook.body:
- Continued investment in Indian railway modernisation, electrification and network expansion is making railway systems more advanced, supporting demand for railway electrical and power-electronics systems.
- A growing policy emphasis on localisation — developing and manufacturing critical railway systems within India — favours domestic engineering suppliers.
- Management expects the need for modern infrastructure, greater electrification and indigenous engineering solutions in the railway sector to remain strong, supported by sustained investment.
- Commercialisation and scale-up of the propulsion business after CLW approval of the three-phase propulsion equipment is the near-term growth lever.
- Order book of approximately ₹1,014 crore, described by the MD as giving strong business visibility for the years ahead.
- At listing, the order book included purchase orders for 450 propulsion systems and a Letter of Acceptance for six MEMU rakes.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: MV Electrosystems designs, develops, assembles and manufactures propulsion systems, electrical equipment, switchgear panels and cable management products for railway rolling stock and the rail electrification network. It operates three segments — Propulsion Equipment, Rail (Overhead) Electrification Products and Switchgear & Cable Protection Products — serving Indian Railways across locomotives, EMUs/MEMUs, metro and Vande Bharat trains. In-house power electronics, embedded systems, software and engineering capability, anchored by a Faridabad R&D Centre, underpins its move from component-level supply towards engineered propulsion systems.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Continued investment in Indian railway modernisation, electrification and network expansion is making railway systems more advanced, supporting demand for railway electrical and power-electronics systems.
- A growing policy emphasis on localisation — developing and manufacturing critical railway systems within India — favours domestic engineering suppliers.
- Management expects the need for modern infrastructure, greater electrification and indigenous engineering solutions in the railway sector to remain strong, supported by sustained investment.
- Commercialisation and scale-up of the propulsion business after CLW approval of the three-phase propulsion equipment is the near-term growth lever.
- Order book of approximately ₹1,014 crore, described by the MD as giving strong business visibility for the years ahead.
- At listing, the order book included purchase orders for 450 propulsion systems and a Letter of Acceptance for six MEMU rakes.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Evolve from a supplier of railway electrical products into an advanced propulsion-technology company, built on the approved indigenous locomotive propulsion system.
- Scale up manufacturing operations to strengthen production capacity, supply-chain resilience and support larger propulsion and rail electrical programmes, complemented by investment in engineering, testing, quality systems, automation and skilled talent.
- Broaden the product and technology portfolio beyond locomotive propulsion into trainsets, distributed power propulsion platforms and other next-generation railway applications, supported by the dedicated R&D Centre.
- Keep indigenous, in-house R&D central: the DSIR-recognised R&D Centre is to be strengthened to develop new products and support long-term growth.
- Deploy IPO proceeds towards operational requirements and investment in research, design and development.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: To execute its order pipeline, the Company is undertaking a scale-up of its manufacturing operations aimed at strengthening production capacity, improving execution capability, enhancing supply-chain resilience and creating infrastructure for larger and more technologically sophisticated propulsion and rail electrical programmes. The Growth Priorities table names capacity expansion through Unit 2 and additional test infrastructure. The scale-up is to be complemented by continued investment in engineering, testing, quality systems, automation and skilled human resources. No project cost, capacity figure or commissioning timeline is stated in this bundle.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- licence/regulatory: RDSO/CLW-approved indigenous IGBT-based 3-phase propulsion equipment for 6,000 HP locomotives — evidence: developed in compliance with CLW standards in September 2025, with commercial supplies to Indian Railways initiated in March 2026 — against it: commercial supplies only began in March 2026, so the approved product has a short supply record
- technology: in-house propulsion IP that reduces dependence on external technology suppliers and royalty payments — evidence: indigenously designed IGBT-based 3-phase drive propulsion system; Faridabad R&D Centre recognised by DSIR in June 2026 with 45 permanent R&D professionals including 35 engineers (21.84% of the permanent workforce)
- customer lock-in: established approved-supplier relationship with Indian Railways — evidence: association since 2009 with a validated compliance and certification history; 76.16% of FY2026 revenue derived from Indian Railways — against it: the same 76.16% is a single-customer concentration

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Dependence on Government railway spending and procurement programmes — The Company flags changes in Government spending priorities, tendering and procurement processes and dependence on customer procurement programmes as risks to its railway-focused business.
- Long development and customer approval cycles — The railway industry involves long development cycles, stringent approvals and customer approval cycles; regulatory complexity and delays in approvals, land acquisition and project permissions can push out schedules and raise operating costs.
- Safety, reliability and standards compliance — Propulsion equipment and cable assemblies must meet rigorous safety and environmental standards and consistently high reliability; failure can cause project delays, higher costs and reputational damage.
- Intense competition for railway contracts — Numerous domestic and international players bid for contracts, and many competitors have strong ties with Indian Railways.
- Supply-chain disruption and electronic component availability/pricing — Raw materials and components come through a global supply chain exposed to geopolitical tensions, natural disasters or pandemics; availability and pricing of critical electronic components can delay production and raise costs.
- Technology change — The Company lists technology changes in the railway sector among its risks, which it seeks to mitigate through continued R&D and product diversification.
